tools.name: research_pain_points
tools.description:
Mode 1 ("The Eyes"): scan GitHub Issues, targeted Reddit subs, and the
public MCP registry for recurring pain points not already solved by an
existing tool; queue anything past the daily mention threshold for
development.

tools.name: develop_tools
tools.description:
Mode 2 ("The Brain"): generate, subprocess-smoke-test, and publish a
tool for every queued backlog item. Publishing writes to
data/tool_registry.json, which both the HTTP dispatcher and this MCP
server's dynamic tool registration read from.

tools.name: check_tool_health
tools.description:
Mode 3 ("The Manager"): deprecate (delete code + registry entry) any
published tool that has earned zero payments after the deprecation
window.

tools.name: run_factory_cycle
tools.description:
Run the full LangGraph-orchestrated pipeline in one call:
research -> develop -> health_check. This is graph.py's only production
entry point -- it is not exposed over HTTP.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: support-ticket-system-friction · Private data: offline-session-sync, add-license-information-to-codebase · Public sink: develop_tools · Destructive: check_tool_health, run_factory_cycle, documentation-creation-toil.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: support-ticket-system-friction · Private data: offline-session-sync, add-license-information-to-codebase · Public sink: develop_tools · Destructive: check_tool_health, run_factory_cycle, documentation-creation-toil

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
